html:
Plymouth Colony was an English colony on the coast of what is now Massachusetts, founded in 1620 by the Pilgrims, religious Separatists who had broken with the Church of England. It lasted until 1691.

They sailed on the Mayflower and signed the Mayflower Compact before landing. They settled at Patuxet, a Wampanoag village emptied by an epidemic a few years before. About half of them died in the first winter. The Nauset had shot at them when they first came ashore, but peace soon followed.

In 1621 Massasoit, the leader of the Pokanoket Wampanoag, made an alliance with them, partly as a balance against the Narragansett. Tisquantum (Squanto), who had learned English after being kidnapped to Europe, helped them farm and trade. Their harvest feast that autumn is remembered as the first Thanksgiving. The governor William Bradford wrote the colony's history.

The colony stayed small and poor beside its larger Puritan neighbour, Massachusetts Bay, founded in 1630. As settlers took more land, relations with the Wampanoag broke down. In King Philip's War of 1675 and 1676, led by Massasoit's son Metacom, both sides suffered terribly, and the Native peoples of southern New England were crushed. In 1691 Plymouth was merged into the Province of Massachusetts Bay.
sum: Plymouth Colony was an English colony on the coast of what is now Massachusetts, founded in 1620 by the Pilgrims, religious Separatists who had broken with the Church of England. It lasted until 1691.
